subject: Different result between fitD.pgls and pairwise

messages.author: 14afb5135d7951b6
messages.subject: Different result between fitD.pgls and pairwise
parts:
Hi,

I hope you can help me clarifying the following issue.

I have a dataset of 102 species with 52 LMs, together with the phylogeny and information on their niche states. When I fit a phylogenetic regression using as predictors the niche states (3 categorical states L, S and H), I obtain the following result:

 fit_pgls <- procD.pgls(Y ~ X, phy = phy, data = gdf, iter = 999)

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals
Number of permutations: 1000
Estimation method: Generalized Least-Squares (via OLS projection)
Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type I
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions

           Df     SS       MS     Rsq      F      Z Pr(>F)  
X         2 0.3190 0.159490 0.07295 3.8951 2.8577  0.002 **
Residuals  99 4.0537 0.040947 0.92705                        
Total     101 4.3727                                        
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Call: procD.lm(f1 = Y ~ X, iter = iter, seed = seed, RRPP = TRUE,  
    SS.type = SS.type, effect.type = effect.type, int.first = int.first,  
    Cov = Cov, data = data, print.progress = print.progress)

Based on this, it seems that when correcting for the phylogenetic relationship between species, the influence of the niche states on shape variation is still significant.

However, if I try to look at the pairwise result, the significance changes:

PW <- pairwise(fit_pgls, groups = X, print.progress = FALSE)
> summary(PW, test.type = "dist", confidence = 0.95)

Pairwise comparisons

Groups: H L S

RRPP: 1000 permutations

LS means:
Vectors hidden (use show.vectors = TRUE to view)

Pairwise distances between means, plus statistics
             d  UCL (95%)          Z Pr > d
H:L 0.07350845 0.09020036  0.8233393  0.193
H:S 0.04307592 0.11184092 -2.2726277  0.986
L:S 0.08245557 0.13227907 -0.4559545  0.682

Does anyone know why this might happen? Is it not correct to fit the function pairwise on a pgls fit?

Thank you very much!

Kind regards,
Silvia

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Different result between fitD.pgls and pairwise
parts:
Silvia,

 

This can happen, even with univariate data (i.e., where a linear model displays a significant effect but pairwise comparisons do not).  The converse is also possible. Please refer to the archives of the geomorph blog, where Mike Collyer addressed this same topic a month or two ago (also, one can go to the Biometry book of Sokal and Rohlf: I seem to recall a similar discussion of this for univariate data back in the day).

 

Dea

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Different result between fitD.pgls and pairwise
parts:
Silvia,

If it has been more than two months since you last updated RRPP, you might wish to update this again:

devtools::install_github(“mlcollyer/RRPP”)

A couple of months ago I did fix a bug with GLS estimation in pairwise.  Although what Dean indicated could be the case, it could also be a problem with the function.  Hard to know since the effect is not very large in ANOVA but it does seem large enough that the really small effect sizes in your pairwise comparisons are suspicious.

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Different result between fitD.pgls and pairwise
parts:
Dear Dean,
Dear Mike,

thank you very much for your replies.

Indeed it was more than two months since I last updated the RRPP package, but even by doing that the result didn't actually changed. The pairwise comparisons are still not significant.

If I understood correctly, this might be due to the fact that the pairwise comparison test is more conservative, while the ANOVA is more sensitive and able to detect difference between the means.

Best regards,
Silvia
